plansAfter.focus: **Sliding windows, linked lists, and first DP.** Two weeks of new patterns: variable-width windows over strings, fast/slow pointers through linked lists, and your first recurrence problems — closing with a Hard window capstone.
plansAfter.notes: Each block ramps inside one family — two window scans, three list problems, two DP problems — so every session adds a single new idea on top of a familiar technique.

items.reason: Two-pointer work is 2/2 (digest), but both solved problems sat on sorted arrays. This is the first variable-width window over a string, testing the pointer discipline without the sorted-array shortcut.

Second sliding-window step, adding a frequency map and an 'at most k replacements' condition. It reuses the hash-map fluency behind the 4/4 arrays-hashing record while forcing the window to shrink dynamically.
First linked-list problem, deliberately Easy: establishes node and pointer mechanics in a new structure before cycles and carry arithmetic.
Transfers the two-pointer skill (2/2) to linked lists — Floyd's fast/slow pointers are the list analogue of a pattern already owned.
Medium list problem pairing traversal with carry bookkeeping; the natural next step after reverse and cycle, adding digit-level state.
Entry point to dynamic programming, the largest untouched topic in the bank. Easy and self-contained, it introduces the recurrence-and-memo framing before array-shaped DP.
First non-trivial recurrence: state depends on the previous two choices. Directly builds on Climbing Stairs and moves DP onto an array, matching your strongest data structure.
Capstone stretch — the bank's only Hard, and untouched. A monotonic deque generalizes the earlier window scans, giving a ceiling now that every attempted Easy and Medium has been solved.

plansAfter.focus: Arrays and hashing week: the complement map family.

# Memory

## Position
- Plan 1 (arrays-hashing complement map, 10d, 4 items) is complete: digest shows solved=4, practiced=0, not_started=0, carried_unsolved=[].
- Advanced to plan 2 (14d, 8 items, based_on=1): sliding window -> linked list -> first DP, with the bank's only Hard as a window capstone.

## Why this block
- Every practiced topic is at 100%: arrays-hashing 4/4, two-pointers 2/2, binary-search 1/1 (digest). Nothing to remediate, so targeting = untouched families + one difficulty step up, not more repetition of solved patterns.
- Difficulty gradient: first exposure to linked lists is Easy (206, 141), then Medium (2); DP starts Easy (70) then Medium (198); the lone Hard (239) is a deliberate end-of-block stretch.
- Pace check: plan 1 created 1788868800000, last session 1789473600000 -> 4 items in 7 days (~4/week). 8 items / 14 days matches that demonstrated pace; previous 10d/4-item plan was light relative to the user's throughput.

## Open threads
- No carries: all plan-1 items solved, so they are retired rather than carried (no carried_from in plan 2).
- No paused/active sessions and none with planItemId=null; nothing outside the plan graph.
- No completed reviews exist (all sessions reviewRequestStatus=null, reviewCount=0; pending queue empty) -> coaching dimension passes vacuously this cycle.
- Reconcile: previous memory said "keep building the same ladder"; the digest contradicts it (ladder fully solved), so this version supersedes that instruction.

## Next-run checks
- Digest adherence on plan 2: any carried_unsolved, and solve_rate on sliding-window / linked-list / dynamic-programming topics.
- Watch for the first completed reviews; if any appear, fold recommended_focus and weaknesses into plan 3 targeting.
- Watch for the first linked-list session (206/141) for pointer bugs or copy-out-before-submit patterns; and whether 239 (Hard) is attempted and how it lands.
- Bank still untouched for future blocks: stacks (20), trees (226, 19), heap (215), prefix-sum (238), plus coin-change (322) and best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock (121) for DP follow-ups.

# Memory
- Plan going well; all items solved.
- Keep building the same ladder next week.
